html:
The Spanish conquest of El Salvador began in 1524, when Pedro de Alvarado marched in from Guatemala, and was completed by about 1539.

Alvarado, fresh from the conquest of the K'iche' in Guatemala, fought the Pipil at Acajutla and Tacuxcalco in 1524 and was wounded in the leg. The Pipil withdrew to the hills and kept up their resistance, and a town called San Salvador was founded in 1525 and refounded several times before it lasted.

Alvarado gave out native towns to his men as encomiendas, rights to tribute and labour. Disease killed many people. The province became part of the Captaincy General of Guatemala within Spanish America and grew indigo for export. The conquest made El Salvador a land of estates and Indigenous labour for four centuries.
sum: The Spanish conquest of El Salvador began in 1524, when Pedro de Alvarado marched in from Guatemala, and was completed by about 1539.
